# How to Check the Default Position Bounds in TaskJointPosVelAccBounds When Only Velocity Bounds Are Configured in TSID?

> **Current answer:** Check if the old constructor sets qMin/qMax as +1e10/-1e10. This order results in qMin > qMax; default explicit setting of position bounds would mask the issue, but setting only velocity bounds may trigger infeasibility. The default values have been merged into PR #159, setting qMin = -1e10 and qMax = +1e10. The old version also needs to be explicitly set to the correct position bounds before use.

## Problem and symptoms

- Why might QP become infeasible when only velocity bounds are configured but the default position bounds are used?
- Default qMin = +1e10, qMax = -1e10; this leads to qMin > qMax; using the default position bounds may result in infeasible constraints.

## Environment

- Old implementation of TSID TaskJointPosVelAccBounds from 2022-03; specific release version and robot model not mentioned.

## Priority diagnostics

- Print or check the qMin/qMax after TaskJointPosVelAccBounds is constructed; confirm if the position bounds are explicitly set before use.

## Possible causes

- The constructor sets qMin and qMax in the wrong order, with the negative sign swapped.

## Attempts

- The questioner identified the constructor code; the maintainer confirmed and requested a PR.

## Effective fixes

- Use merged PR #159, setting qMin = -1e10 and qMax = +1e10; the old version can also explicitly set the correct position bounds to avoid relying on the incorrect default values.
